findings.title: Round 2's shots.js change crashes the test: test/shots.js always exits 1, so CI fails and no section 6 page check runs
findings.location: rex-strength-lab/test/shots.js line 582 (added in a7b9db6, the test for brief-2/code-1/copy-4)
findings.evidence:
Line 582 now reads `growHead[st.grow] = await page.evaluate(() => (...).textContent || '').replace(/ /g, ' ');`, and the 'Item' line has the same form. `await` binds looser than the member call, so `.replace` is called on the Promise that page.evaluate returns. A clean clone at a7b9db6 builds with git status clean, then `node test/shots.js` gets through the views, the saved states, the powers and the first two section 6 checks and stops with:
'TypeError: page.evaluate(...).replace is not a function
    at .../rex-strength-lab/test/shots.js:582:467'
Exit code 1 (scratchpad/reviewC3/fixes/shots-real.log; also fullrun.log). This always happens, not only on some runs. At 4656cb3 the line had no .replace, so the crash is new in a7b9db6. The Weight-tab rule check, the growth one-figure check, the milestone check and the sources-table check never run. Round 2 recorded 'shots.js checks the line and the table' (brief-2) and 'shots.js checks it' (brief-3) as outcomes, but neither check can run. In CI (.github/workflows/test.yml) the 'Rex lab - page screenshots' step fails. GitHub then skips the powers.js and ladder.js steps after it, and CLAUDE.md rule 3 blocks the merge.
findings.expected: test/shots.js runs to the end and exits 0 on the branch, and the new section 6 checks really run.
findings.fix: Put the await in parentheses: `growHead[st.grow] = (await page.evaluate(() => ...)).replace(/ /g, ' ');`, and the same for `growHead[st.grow + 'Item']`. Or do the replace inside the evaluated function, as the 'Table' line already does. Checked in a scratch harness that is section 6 of shots.js verbatim with only this change (scratchpad/reviewC3/fixes/sec6-full.js). On the branch build it passes and exits 0, with all six section 6 checks ok. On a copy with growthItems' rough flag and the milestone's rough flag reverted, it fails both checks ('It becomes 5.82 kg', '5,560 t', '10.7 m tall'; 'impact785 quintillion t'). On a copy with the table's mass rounding reverted, it fails ('5,570 t (1,900×)'). Then run the whole test line again.

verdict.reasoning: The crash was real at a7b9db6 but is already fixed at the branch head, 26b62c9 ('shots.js: fix the growth what-if text capture (the replace ran on the promise)', pushed: local and origin/claude/rex-gui-c match). At head, lines 582-588 use a textOf helper that runs the replace inside page.evaluate, so .replace never runs on a Promise. A head copy builds byte-identical to the repo's data.js and dist/index.html. Its full shots.js runs to the end and exits 0 in 6m18s, and every section 6 check runs and passes: the growth one-figure check, the milestone and the sources table. The fixed check also works: with growthItems' rough flag forced off (mutant mC), it fails ('krakatoaItem':'It becomes 5.82 kg of new mass...', exit 1). The defect is not on the branch as it stands, so it is not counted. Severity at a7b9db6 would have been major (CI red).
verdict.reproduction: S=scratchpad/reviewC3/verify-fixes. (1) git archive a7b9db6 into $S/a7b, then build-data.py, build.js and node test/shots.js. Output ($S/a7b-shots.log): 'ok each Compared with tile is the ladder's wording...', then 'TypeError: page.evaluate(...).replace is not a function at .../a7b/rex-strength-lab/test/shots.js:582:467', EXIT 1. (2) git archive 26b62c9 (head) into $S/head. Its build cmp-matches the repo's src/data.js and dist/index.html. node test/shots.js ($S/head-shots.log): 62 ok lines, including 'ok growth what-if gives the rough Krakatoa and dinosaur-killer energies...', 'ok the dinosaur-killer milestone is given roughly: ...about 800 quintillion t', 'ok the sources table lists all 58 energy rungs...', with real 6m17.656s and EXIT 0. (3) Mutant mC (head with `const rough = false;` in growthItems), run through section 6 only ($S/mC/rex-strength-lab/test/sec6.js): 'PROBLEM growth what-if: rough energies should be given to one figure: {... "krakatoaItem":"It becomes 5.82 kg of new mass..."', EXIT 1.

findings.title: The growth check covers only the table's Mass column and the item's mass and height: rounding the table's height and density and the item's density can be reverted and the test still passes
findings.location: rex-strength-lab/test/shots.js lines 589-594 (twoFig and the chicxulubItem regex)
findings.evidence: Mutant mB (scratchpad/reviewC3/fixes/mB) undoes round 2's rounding of the Height and Density table cells (`fmtDist(gB.H)`, `fmtDensity2(gB.rho)`) and of the density in growthItems. With the crash from fixes-1 fixed (sec6-fast.js), the check prints 'ok growth what-if gives the rough Krakatoa and dinosaur-killer energies, and the masses they make, to one figure'. Yet the page now reads '... so he is about 11 m tall at 45,600 kg/m³'. twoFig scans only `td[data-col="Mass"]`. The item regex forbids 3-figure masses and heights ('\d,\d*[1-9]\d* t|\d\.\d+ m tall') but not densities. Round 2's outcome says the table's figures and the item's height and density are rounded and that 'shots.js checks the line and the table'.
findings.expected: Each figure round 2 rounded for a rough rung has a check that fails when its rounding is removed.
findings.fix: In shots.js, collect all of the dinosaur-killer table's cells (Mass, Height, Density), not just Mass, and require two significant figures at most in each changed figure. For example, apply twoFig's digit count to '([\d.,]+) m' and '([\d.,]+)(?: × 10[⁰-⁹]+)? kg/m³' too, skipping the unchanged '3.05 m' and '1,060 kg/m³'. Extend the item regex to forbid '\d,\d*[1-9]\d* kg/m³'.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced on the branch head (after 26b62c9). The growth check in shots.js reads only td[data-col="Mass"] for the table (twoFig). The item regex /\d,\d*[1-9]\d* t|\d\.\d+ m tall/ catches 3-figure masses and heights but not densities. Mutant mB reverts round 2's rounding of the Height and Density table cells and of the item's density. The page then shows the 3-figure '10.7 m', '45,600 kg/m³' and '37.4 m' in the table and '...about 11 m tall at 45,600 kg/m³' in the item, and section 6 still passes all six checks, exit 0. Round 2 recorded brief-2's outcome as 'the table rounds each figure the growth changes by 10% or more to two figures ... shots.js checks the line and the table'. The check covers only part of that. This is a test-coverage gap; the page itself is right at head.
verdict.reproduction: S=scratchpad/reviewC3/verify-fixes. mB = the head copy with `fmtDist(r2(gB.H, c.body.H))` changed to `fmtDist(gB.H)`, `fmtDensity2(r2(gB.rho, c.body.rho))` changed to `fmtDensity2(gB.rho)`, and the item's rough density changed to `fmtDensity2(gB.rho)`; rebuilt. node grow-probe.js on mB's dist ($S/grow-mB.out): table 'MIX (DEFAULT) 5,600 t (1,900×) 10.7 m 45,600 kg/m³ / PURE SIZE 5,600 t (1,900×) 37.4 m'; item '...so he is about 11 m tall at 45,600 kg/m³'. node test/sec6.js in mB (shots.js lines 1-35 and 531-616, verbatim; $S/mB-sec6.log): all six 'ok', including 'ok growth what-if gives the rough Krakatoa and dinosaur-killer energies, and the masses they make, to one figure', EXIT 0. The stronger check below ($S/fix2-check.js) prints 'head tableOK true itemOK true' and 'mB tableOK false itemOK false'.
verdict.better_fix:
In test/shots.js section 6:
(1) Capture every table cell: `growHead[st.grow + 'Table'] = await textOf('#bay .growth-whatif td[data-col]', '.');`
(2) Replace twoFig with a check that allows only his unchanged body figures to keep 3 figures:
`const sigf = (s) => s.replace(/[,.]/g, '').replace(/^0+/, '').replace(/0+$/, '').length;
const twoFig = (t) => t.split(' | ').every((c) => c === '3.05 m' || c === '1,060 kg/m³' || !/^[\d.,]+/.test(c) || sigf(c.match(/^[\d.,]+/)[0]) <= 2);`
(3) Extend the item regex to `/\d,\d*[1-9]\d* t|\d\.\d+ m tall|\d,\d*[1-9]\d* kg\/m³/`.
This was checked on the head page's strings (passes) and on mB's (fails).

findings.outcome: Fixed: the check reads every table cell (each is his unchanged figure or at most two figures), forbids a three-figure density in the growth sentence, and needs the rough note.

findings.title: The growth what-if's other lines for a rough rung still give 3 figures, which contradicts the README's new statement that 'where a rough rung sets another number, that number is rough too'
findings.location: rex-strength-lab/src/app.html growthItems (lines 1152-1188: the gradual, instant and runaway items); rex-strength-lab/README.md Known limits, 'Energy comparisons' bullet
findings.evidence: Probe (scratchpad/reviewC3/fixes/probe/grow.js, grow-1280.out): Weight tab, Dinosaur-killer impact chip, absorb gradual. 'It becomes about 6,000 t of new mass ... about 11 m tall at about 46,000 kg/m³', then 'Shortest harmless time: 91.5 s ... The air alone would allow 920 ms', '... rises at up to 0.381 m/s'. With absorb instant or runaway: 'his sides move out at about 317 m/s and the top of his head rises at 1,100 m/s (Mach 3.2)', 'The air at his surface jumps by 125 kPa–781 kPa. As a blast that is 7.1 kg TNT to 44 kg TNT: windows break out to about 25.8 m–90 m', 'his middle rises 3.82 m', 'enough to throw him about 15.4 km up', '3.1 billion kg·m/s', '403 J here'. Every one of these is set by the rough 5 × 10²³ J, whose published spread runs to 1.7 × 10²⁵ J. At 1.674e25 J the engine gives a mix height of about 19 m, not 10.7 m. 'his middle rises 3.82 m', just under 'about 11 m tall', is the 3-figure (10.68 − 3.048)/2. The page's own sources row gives the same time as 'Chicxulub about 1½ min (mix)'. README (added in 4656cb3): 'Where a rough rung sets another number, that number is rough too: the growth what-if gives the Krakatoa and dinosaur-killer energies, and the mass they make, to one figure ...'.
findings.expected: In the what-if box for a rough rung, the numbers derived from its energy are given roughly (1–2 figures, or marked as rough), as the mass, height and density now are. Or the README states only what the page does.
findings.fix: In growthItems, when opts.rough is set, round the derived figures to 2 significant figures before formatting: G.T, G.Tp, u, I.u, I.uHead, I.dpLo/I.dpHi, I.Elo/I.Ehi and the window distances, I.rise, I.sink, I.launchWould, RW.Egrav, the momentum. For example, use `const r2 = (x) => (rough ? Number(x.toPrecision(2)) : x)` and wrap each argument of fmtTime, speedOnly, fmtSI, fmtTNT and fmtDist. Alternatively, add one line to the box: 'Every figure below is as rough as the asteroid’s energy (uncertain by more than 10×)'. In the README, narrow the sentence to what is rounded.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced at head. With a growth mode on and the dinosaur-killer chip picked, the box gives the rough rung's mass, height and density roughly ('about 6,000 t', 'about 11 m tall at about 46,000 kg/m³'). Every later line, all set by the same energy, is still given to 3 figures with nothing marking it rough. In gradual mode: 'Shortest harmless time: 91.5 s', 'The air alone would allow 920 ms', '0.381 m/s'. In instant and runaway modes: '317 m/s', '125 kPa–781 kPa', '25.8 m–90 m', '15.4 km up', '403 J here'. The clearest clash is 'about 11 m tall' followed two lines later by 'his middle rises 3.82 m', which is (10.68 − 3.048)/2 from the unrounded height. The published spread runs to 1.7e25 J, where the engine gives H = 19.2 m and a rise of 8.06 m. This is the same defect round 2 accepted as brief-2 and code-1 (round to what the data supports), left in the box's other lines. Minor: the arithmetic is right, and the box does carry the 'Disputed' note.

I rate it minor, not major: every figure is a rounded form of a correct value marked 'about', and the physics is right.
